note: Header and Footer Scripts stores site-wide CSS/JS in three plain config objects, each with a 'styles' string and a 'scripts' string: header_and_footer_scripts.header.settings (rendered into <head> via hook_page_attachments_alter), .body.settings (after <body> via hook_page_top), .footer.settings (near end via hook_page_bottom). Configure route header_and_footer_scripts.admin.header at /admin/config/development/header-and-footer-scripts/{header,body,footer}; permission header_and_footer_scripts_settings. No config schema. Medium cases read a known marker written into a region config; hard cases require writing a specific snippet into a region config, verified by reading the live config value. Baseline is 'config objects absent', restored by deleting them.

evals.prompt: I want to add a site-wide Google Analytics / GA4 tracking snippet to every page of my Drupal 11 site without editing theme files. The header_and_footer_scripts module is enabled. Where do I put the script and where is it stored?
evals.expected_output: Go to Configuration -> Development -> Header Footer Scripts (/admin/config/development/header-and-footer-scripts/header) and paste the <script> into the Scripts textarea of the Header form; it saves to config header_and_footer_scripts.header.settings (key 'scripts') and is injected into <head> via hook_page_attachments_alter().

evals.prompt: The header_and_footer_scripts module offers three regions to inject scripts/styles. Name the three regions and where each one renders in the page markup, and give the config object for each.
evals.expected_output: Header (header_and_footer_scripts.header.settings) -> injected into <head> (hook_page_attachments_alter). Body (header_and_footer_scripts.body.settings) -> printed right after the opening <body> tag (hook_page_top), the right spot for a Google Tag Manager <noscript>. Footer (header_and_footer_scripts.footer.settings) -> printed near the end of the page (hook_page_bottom). Each object has a 'styles' and a 'scripts' string.

evals.prompt: Which permission controls who can edit the Header and Footer Scripts settings forms in Drupal, and what is its human label?
must_contain_any: Add Scripts all over the site
evals.expected_output: The single permission header_and_footer_scripts_settings, labelled 'Add Scripts all over the site' (marked restricted). It gates all three region settings forms (header/body/footer).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the header_and_footer_scripts module has an inline script configured in one of its regions. Inspect the live configuration and report the distinctive marker string inside that script.
evals.expected_output: The header region config header_and_footer_scripts.header.settings has scripts set to a <script> that logs HFS_MARKER_ABC123.

evals.prompt: The header_and_footer_scripts module on this site has a custom <style> block configured in its footer region. Inspect the live configuration and report the CSS class used in that style block.
evals.expected_output: Config header_and_footer_scripts.footer.settings has styles set to a <style> block targeting the class .hfs-footer-marker-xyz.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the header_and_footer_scripts module to add this exact inline script to the FOOTER region so it renders near the bottom of every page: <script>console.log("HFS goodbye 42");</script>. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set the 'scripts' key of config header_and_footer_scripts.footer.settings to the given <script> snippet (via the Footer settings form or configFactory getEditable('header_and_footer_scripts.footer.settings')->set('scripts', ...)->save()). Verify checks the footer config's scripts contains 'HFS goodbye 42'.

evals.prompt: I need this exact analytics snippet to load in the <head> of every page on my site, using the tool that adds scripts site-wide from the admin UI: <script>console.log("HFS head hi 7");</script>. Please set it up on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set the 'scripts' key of config header_and_footer_scripts.header.settings to the given <script> (Header settings form). The header region renders into <head> via hook_page_attachments_alter(). Verify checks the header config's scripts contains 'HFS head hi 7'.
